title: Consolidate GPU provisioning interfaces and introduce lightweight scheduler
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Over time the GPU fleet codebase accrued multiple provisioning interfaces (lease pool APIs, direct provision callers, and a legacy reconciliation loop). This has increased cognitive load, led to duplicated edge cases during node teardown, and caused intermittent double-provision bursts under cache-thrash workloads.

Goal: Reduce surface area by consolidating provisioning entrypoints into a single Provisioner API and add a lightweight, rate-aware scheduler that performs quick, in-memory decisions for short-lived bursts. The consolidated code should make node lifecycle transitions explicit, minimize cross-component locking, and enable future event-sourced state.

Scope:
- Replace legacy LeasePool client calls used by autoscaler and capacity planner with a single Provisioner facade.
- Extract and isolate node lifecycle state transitions (PENDING -> PROVISIONING -> READY -> DRAINING -> TERMINATED) into a small finite-state machine with explicit transition handlers.
- Implement a lightweight scheduler for short windows (<30s) to handle burst provisioning decisions that avoids the full capacity planner path.
- Maintain a compatibility shim for Dedicated customers and preserve metrics and audit events.
- No infrastructure changes (no fleet API changes to operators) — infra compatibility is required.
acceptance_criteria: Provisioner facade exists and is the only exported API used by capacity planner and autoscaler for node provisioning requests
Unit and integration tests cover all explicit lifecycle transitions and failure/retry behavior
Benchmarks show reduction in median provisioning latency for burst allocations by >= 25% under synthetic workload
No increase in provisioning-related errors in staging for 72-hour soak (measured via error-rate and reconciliations-per-node metrics)
Compatibility shim returns identical audit events and metrics for Dedicated customers within current retention
rollout_plan: Feature branch implements Provisioner and lightweight scheduler behind feature flag 'provisioner_v2'
Deploy to alpha region and run workload generator emulating bursty tenant traffic for 24h
Enable flag for 10% of production autoscaler traffic and monitor reconcile/lease churn metrics for 48h
Increment rollout to 50% then 100% if no regressions; rollback immediately on error-rate spike or >10% increase in duplicate provisions
Remove compatibility shim and legacy provisioner code after 2 sustained releases with zero incidents
migration_steps: Step 1: Add Provisioner facade implementation alongside existing APIs; wire autoscaler to call facade when feature flag enabled
Step 2: Implement and test FSM for node lifecycle; run unit tests and integration tests in CI
Step 3: Introduce lightweight scheduler that consults an in-memory view and defers to capacity planner on ambiguous cases
Step 4: Enable feature flag behind canary toggle; monitor metrics and incrementally shift traffic
Step 5: Deprecate legacy entrypoints and remove dead code after metrics validate behavior
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: New facade could introduce latency regressions if it performs synchronous remote calls - Mitigation: keep hot path in-memory and use async background reconciliation
Risk: Behavioral drift for Dedicated customers - Mitigation: compatibility shim that mirrors prior audit events and exposes 'compat-check' logs
Risk: Edge-case race during node teardown leading to duplicate provisions - Mitigation: add idempotency keys and reconcile-on-read in FSM
Risk: Tests insufficient for rare failure modes - Mitigation: create chaos test harness that simulates cloud API errors and timeouts
qa_plan: Unit tests for Provisioner functions and FSM transitions
Integration tests against simulated cloud resource allocator
Staging soak with workload generator for 72 hours before canary
Canary in prod with tight alerting: reconciliations-per-node, duplicate_provision_count, median_provision_latency
Post-rollout smoke validating metrics and alerting rules
observability_changes: Trace additions: distributed trace span 'provisioner.decision' capturing call path and idempotency key
Dashboards: provisioning heatmap and reconciliation churn per pool
